quickAnswer: The C2PA Content Credentials Viewer inspects JPEG, PNG, WebP, and AVIF media files for embedded Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) manifests. It parses JPEG Universal Metadata Box Format (JUMBF) containers in browser memory to reveal the issuing signing authority, software claim generator (Adobe Photoshop, DALL-E, Midjourney, Leica), editing history, and AI source classifications. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device with no server uploads.

faq.q: What is C2PA and Content Credentials?
faq.a: C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) is an open technical standard developed by Adobe, Microsoft, Intel, and the BBC. It embeds tamper-evident cryptographic manifests into media files, recording who created the file, what software generated or modified it, and whether artificial intelligence was used [Confirmed: C2PA Technical Specifications].

faq.q: How does C2PA detect AI-generated imagery?
faq.a: AI generators that adhere to C2PA standards (such as OpenAI DALL-E 3, Midjourney, and Adobe Firefly) sign an assertion called digitalSourceType set to 'trainedAlgorithmicMedia' or 'compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia'. This assertion is cryptographically sealed into the file manifest.

faq.q: Can C2PA metadata be stripped from an image?
faq.a: Yes. If an image is screenshotted, re-compressed through social media apps (Twitter/X, Facebook) that strip metadata, or converted via basic image converters, the C2PA container is discarded. However, any modification to a C2PA-bearing image without re-signing breaks cryptographic hash validation, immediately flagging the manifest as modified.

faq.q: Does this tool upload my photos to any third-party verification server?
faq.a: No. The entire JUMBF binary box traversal, FourCC scanning, and assertion parsing run locally in your browser memory using an ArrayBuffer parser. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device.

articleHtml:
Understanding C2PA Provenance: JUMBF Box Format, Manifests, and AI Attributions

With the exponential proliferation of generative artificial intelligence, cryptographic content provenance standards like C2PA provide verifiable mathematical evidence of an asset's authoring history, modification chain, and authentic origin.

JPEG Universal Metadata Box Format (JUMBF) Containers

C2PA standardizes on the ISO/IEC 19566-5 JUMBF architecture to embed structured binary payloads inside image and video containers without breaking backward compatibility for standard media players:

  • JPEG APP11 Markers: In JPEG files, C2PA manifests are broken across 64KB segments marked by 0xFFEB (APP11) with the JP2C or c2pa marker.
  • PNG Chunks: Stored within specialized ancillary chunks (caIp or c2pa).
  • WebP RIFF Chunks: Stored within a four-character code (FourCC) chunk named C2PA.

AI Source Assertions: trainedAlgorithmicMedia

The C2PA specification establishes standard assertion vocabularies to identify synthesis methods:

$$\text{Assertion} = \{ \text{"digitalSourceType"}: \text{"http://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia"} \}$$

When systems like OpenAI DALL-E, Midjourney, or Adobe Firefly export imagery, they sign this assertion using an X.509 certificate rooted in an approved trust list (such as the C2PA Trust List managed by the Content Authenticity Initiative). Modifying or tampering with pixels without re-signing the manifest invalidates the cryptographic SHA-256 hash tree.

Security & Privacy Notice: All file reading, binary FourCC inspection, and provenance parsing occur locally in browser memory. Inputs are not uploaded to our servers. ToolkitGen is an independent platform.
